about: Where the Department of Defense sends its contract dollars, per resident, and what a state produces per resident, for all 56 places. Used to size how far a defense build-up reaches each place.

sources.contracts: USAspending.gov API, POST /api/v2/search/spending_by_geography/, awarding agency Department of Defense, contract award types A-D, fiscal year 2024 (October 1, 2023 to September 30, 2024), place of performance by state, transaction level, read September 29, 2026
sources.nationalByYear: USAspending.gov API, POST /api/v2/search/spending_over_time/, same filters, fiscal years 2008 to 2024, read September 29, 2026
sources.gdp: Bureau of Economic Analysis, SAGDP1 line 3, current-dollar GDP, 2024, https://apps.bea.gov/regional/zip/SAGDP.zip, read September 29, 2026
sources.prices: BLS CPI-U, U.S. city average, all items, annual average (1982-84=100), used to put fiscal-year dollars in one price level

multiplier.meaning: dollars of extra output in a state for each extra dollar of procurement spent there, relative to other states
multiplier.source: Nakamura and Steinsson 2014, "Fiscal Stimulus in a Monetary Union: Evidence from U.S. Regions", NBER w17391 (open-economy relative multiplier about 1.5, from military build-ups and draw-downs across regions)

buildUp.meaning: How fast defense contracts grew, in real terms, in the fiscal years they beat inflation. A defense law that grows spending faster than inflation carries this pace until the run ends.
buildUp.note: Fiscal-year contract dollars are deflated with calendar-year CPI-U averages, so the pace is an estimate to about a point.
